action.name: Typed pad-absent HyperBoost reversible validation
action.value: Balanced mode 0 to HyperBoost mode 7 on both channels, immediate typed readback, then exact Balanced restoration with pad USB and external power operator-confirmed disconnected; no dwell or load

validation.applyResult: Applied successfully: both mode-7 setters were acknowledged while the cooling pad was physically absent.
validation.readbackResult: Readback confirmed mode 7/value 0 independently on both thermal channels.
validation.restorationResult: Restored successfully: the saved Balanced pair was submitted once and acknowledged on both channels.
validation.restorationReadbackResult: Restoration readback confirmed the exact saved mode 0/value 0 state on both channels.

sanitizedEvidence.summary: The validator confirmed the exact laptop and BIOS, inactive competing controllers, inactive OpenBlade service, two preliminary command-level absence samples 500 ms apart, the full-power 280 W adapter state, two identical paired Balanced/Automatic laptop reads, and operator confirmation that both pad power sources were disconnected.

Inside the exclusive laptop session, the validator performed a third exact-pad absence observation immediately before the writes and reconfirmed full-power eligibility. It did not continuously monitor pad absence or perform a post-restoration absence observation.

The validator submitted exactly one mode-7 write per channel, received both acknowledgements, independently confirmed the paired HyperBoost state, then restored and independently confirmed the exact saved Balanced state without dwell or load.
The elevated wrapper bound the exact Capture executable, recorded the sanitized semantic result, reported an empty stderr and no wrapper failure, and restored both temporarily stopped Razer services.
sanitizedEvidence.wrapperCompletionTimeSource: elevated wrapper report file completion metadata

limitations: This single exact-device run proves only that the immediate firmware transition and restoration were accepted and readable after three pad-absence observations before mutation and operator confirmation that both cooling-pad power sources were physically disconnected.
Pad absence was not monitored continuously and was not observed again after restoration.
No dwell, benchmark, sustained workload, power-limit measurement, component-temperature trend, or long-duration thermal validation was performed.
The result does not establish that pad-less HyperBoost is thermally safe or suitable for production use, and it does not remove the existing cooling-pad presence gate.
The result does not expand support to another laptop model, firmware version, power-adapter state, or cooling-pad fan operation.
The private typed transcript and elevated wrapper report remain uncommitted.

productionAdmission.reason: One exact-build no-load run showed that the laptop accepted HyperBoost, returned typed paired mode-7 readback, and restored Balanced after three pad-absence observations before mutation. The validator itself kept production admission false, and this run does not establish continuous absence, load or thermal safety, lifecycle behavior, or production-service eligibility.

notes: capturedAtUtc records the elevated wrapper report completion time from file metadata; the validator did not emit its own timestamp.
USBPcap was not running during the typed validation.
The installed OpenBlade service remained stopped and was not restarted.
Razer Game Manager Service 3 and Razer Elevation Service were restored after the bounded run.
